name: Publish npm

on:
  push:
    tags:
      - "v*"
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions: {}

concurrency:
  group: publish-npm-${{ github.ref_name }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  publish:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      id-token: write
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@11bd71901bbe5b1630ceea73d27597364c9af683 # v4.2.2
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Setup Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@39370e3970a6d050c480ffad4ff0ed4d3fdee5af # v4.1.0
        with:
          node-version: "22"
          registry-url: "https://registry.npmjs.org"
          cache: npm

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci --ignore-scripts

      - name: Build (no packages/ai generate-models)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          npx tsgo -p packages/tui/tsconfig.build.json
          npx tsgo -p packages/ai/tsconfig.build.json
          npx tsgo -p packages/agent/tsconfig.build.json
          npm --prefix packages/coding-agent run build

      - name: Publish @ashx-j/lunr*
        run: node scripts/publish.mjs
        env:
          NODE_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}

# lunR qualified-PR review findings

Date: 2026-09-26. Review target: `b57c148`, local `origin/master`, through PR #115 and version 0.2.24.

## Scope and method

Five heavy subagents reviewed and tested separate areas: subagents/permissions, TUI/settings, providers/startup, gateway/packaging, and imported pi extensions. This report consolidates their evidence. No fixes were applied.

The historical filter selected 68 PRs: 26 Grok-attributed and 42 without identifiable model attribution. PR #96 was added for its outstanding gateway verification. Named models count as attribution even without a provider-qualified slash slug. Anthropic subscription work, including #107 and its portions of release integrations, was excluded at the user's request. Native computer use and unmerged remote hosting were excluded.

The original checkout is a dirty, older branch at `e36432c`. Reviewers were redirected to a clean detached checkout at `../lunR-review-audit`. Its final git status was clean. Existing working files, installed CLI, credentials, services, and GitHub state were not changed. No live provider requests, bot messages, installations, publication, or reboot checks were performed.

Tests target current surviving behavior, not every historical branch. Release PRs share current integration checks. Removed code and superseded unmerged work receive a disposition instead of redundant testing. Source mocks established the defects below; the suite counts alone are not proof of full feature qualification.

The review checkout uses junctioned dependencies. Coding-agent Vitest aliases use source, but other imports can resolve older compiled workspace dependencies. No isolated production build or current compiled-CLI acceptance was performed. Do not interpret this report as a release certification.

## Later-PR reconciliation

Two standard subagents checked every finding against merged history, current source and the live GitHub PR API on 2026-09-26. Stable master remains `b57c148`. PRs #77 and #116 through #119 are open. No finding below has a verified later merged fix. This pass inspected code and tests without rerunning suites; original execution counts remain unchanged.

Two open proposals matter: [#118](https://github.com/ashx-j/lunR/pull/118/files), head `43e06c7`, proposes the OpenCode classification fix; [#119](https://github.com/ashx-j/lunR/pull/119/files), head `09d6705`, partially addresses gateway outbox handling. Both target master. Do not duplicate their proposed work or treat it as shipped.

| Issue | Later-PR status |
| --- | --- |
| R1 | Still present. No later fix found for alternate Node flags or package-script execution. |
| R2 | Still present. Explicit async SINGLE exclusion remains unchanged. |
| R3 | Still present. Provider-only cache keys and stale in-flight completion remain unchanged. |
| R4 | Still present on master. Open #119 drops obsolete notices, but explicitly retains completed results across session changes. The remaining result policy needs a product decision. |
| P1 | Still present. No later removal or cleanup of the process-wide exception handler. |
| P2 | Still present. Both command registrations remain. |
| P3 | All OAuth, MCP client and host identity subitems remain; no live qualification added. |
| P4 | All four tool-description, setup and watchdog branding subitems remain. |
| P5 | Security docs, gallery guidance, all cited examples and migration links remain. |
| P6 | All three dormant comment/path subitems remain; none is promoted to a runtime-write claim. |
| T1 | Still present. Neither later relevant PR repairs the missing runtimeHost mocks. |
| T2a | xAI stale assertion remains untouched. |
| T2b | Reclassified as a medium catalog-generation defect, not merely a stale fixture. Open #118 proposes its fix and focused assertions; not merged. |
| T3 settings | Old .pi settings fixtures remain; #118 does not change these files. |
| T3 resource lists | Existing path/list expectation failures remain; #118 does not address them. |
| T3 footer | Windows separator expectation remains unchanged. |
| T3 model instructions | Remains an unresolved test-contract disagreement, not a confirmed runtime defect. |
| D1 | Still present, including in open #119 despite adjacent gateway documentation changes. |
| Packaging | npm 12 output-shape limitation remains. No release failure or later fix established. |
| Compatibility inventory | Workspace names, pi API names, legacy reads/migration and share viewer remain intentional. Codex originator-header requirement remains unverified. |

Historical replacements such as #28 -> #30, #61 -> #62 and the UI reversals in #68 were already accounted for in the PR disposition table. Changes merged before the reproduced `b57c148` behavior do not close these current findings. Open dev-channel work is not a stable fix.

## Priority findings

### R1. High: read-only Bash classification allows executable command forms

Locations: `packages/coding-agent/src/core/plan-mode.ts:117-160,361-369`.

The command classifier blocks a short list of package-manager operations and exact Node flag strings. Source-level calls to `gateToolCall("bash", ...)` allowed these forms in read-only mode:

- `node --eval=0`
- `npm run build`
- `pnpm run build`
- `yarn run build`
- `npm exec -- echo ok`

The reviewer classified strings only and did not execute those commands. These forms can execute arbitrary code or project scripts that write files. The source explicitly describes its heuristic as not a security boundary, so this is a gap in advertised read-only enforcement, not a claim of an OS sandbox escape.

Existing permission tests do not cover these inputs. A follow-up should define the intended shell contract and test alternate flag syntax and package-script execution against it.

### R2. Medium: explicit async SINGLE calls skip aggregate launch approval

Locations: `packages/coding-agent/src/core/large-subagent-launch.ts:13-15,33-35,48-61`; async default in `src/builtin-extensions/pi-subagents/src/runs/background/top-level-async.ts:24-27`.

Three same-turn SINGLE calls with `async:true` were excluded from the large-launch count. In yolo mode with confirmation enabled and a registered rejecting approval handler, a source reproduction returned count `0`, three allowed gate results, and zero prompts. Omitting `async` for the same trio counted three, although omission now also means async execution.

No children were launched. The explicit and omitted forms should have the same approval behavior. Relevant history includes #23, #24, #47 and later async integration carried by #86.

### R3. Medium: provider-only usage cache mixes account results

Locations: `packages/coding-agent/src/core/usage-service.ts:119-153,182-185`; cache clearing callers in `src/core/model-runtime.ts:620,632,641`.

Cached and pending requests are keyed only by provider. A mocked Kimi source reproduction returned account A's 10% usage for account B with only one fetch. A second reproduction cleared the cache, fetched B's 30%, then completed A's older pending request. Subsequent B usage reverted to 10%.

Login/logout cache clearing does not invalidate outstanding completions. Wrong quota can remain visible for the 60-second TTL, including across account changes. No credentials or network requests were used. Follow-up coverage should exercise account identity and stale in-flight completion after invalidation. Relevant PRs include #5, #19 and #31.

Locations: `packages/coding-agent/src/core/plan-mode.ts:117-160,361-369`.

The command classifier blocks a short list of package-manager operations and exact Node flag strings. Source-level calls to `gateToolCall("bash", ...)` allowed these forms in read-only mode:

- `node --eval=0`
- `npm run build`
- `pnpm run build`
- `yarn run build`
- `npm exec -- echo ok`

The reviewer classified strings only and did not execute those commands. These forms can execute arbitrary code or project scripts that write files. The source explicitly describes its heuristic as not a security boundary, so this is a gap in advertised read-only enforcement, not a claim of an OS sandbox escape.

Existing permission tests do not cover these inputs. A follow-up should define the intended shell contract and test alternate flag syntax and package-script execution against it.

### R2. Medium: explicit async SINGLE calls skip aggregate launch approval

Locations: `packages/coding-agent/src/core/large-subagent-launch.ts:13-15,33-35,48-61`; async default in `src/builtin-extensions/pi-subagents/src/runs/background/top-level-async.ts:24-27`.

Three same-turn SINGLE calls with `async:true` were excluded from the large-launch count. In yolo mode with confirmation enabled and a registered rejecting approval handler, a source reproduction returned count `0`, three allowed gate results, and zero prompts. Omitting `async` for the same trio counted three, although omission now also means async execution.

No children were launched. The explicit and omitted forms should have the same approval behavior. Relevant history includes #23, #24, #47 and later async integration carried by #86.

### R3. Medium: provider-only usage cache mixes account results

Locations: `packages/coding-agent/src/core/usage-service.ts:119-153,182-185`; cache clearing callers in `src/core/model-runtime.ts:620,632,641`.

Cached and pending requests are keyed only by provider. A mocked Kimi source reproduction returned account A's 10% usage for account B with only one fetch. A second reproduction cleared the cache, fetched B's 30%, then completed A's older pending request. Subsequent B usage reverted to 10%.

Login/logout cache clearing does not invalidate outstanding completions. Wrong quota can remain visible for the 60-second TTL, including across account changes. No credentials or network requests were used. Follow-up coverage should exercise account identity and stale in-flight completion after invalidation. Relevant PRs include #5, #19 and #31.

  "body": "Native computer use sends bounded screenshots instead of large accessibility-tree observations. Crops help with small controls, and each input call returns one post-action image. Hardware verification below is Windows x64 only.\n- Exact-target, single-use observations with a 30-second lifetime, crop coordinate mapping, bounded metadata and guards against repeated unchanged input.\n- Pre-dispatch rejection reports that the call sent no input. The fresh screenshot showed six characters, proving partial delivery. The tool reported uncertain input and confirmed cleanup. The native process exited and the desktop lease released before a new workflow successfully captured the same window. Final shutdown stopped the new native process and released its lease too.\n- Ubuntu CI is not clean. At reviewed head `66e1a12`, the complete job log has exactly the same 98 failing test names across 24 suites as the #118 baseline, with zero new failures. Agent passes 181 tests, AI passes 623 with 760 skips, and coding-agent passes 2815 with 98 failures and 55 skips. Broader Ubuntu cleanup remains outside this update. CI for the subsequent Unicode boundary fix is separate from those completed results.\n\n## Independent delta review\n\nA fresh heavy read-only reviewer examined the named-app discovery and Windows foreground-shortcut changes from `217a98e` through `66e1a12`, separately from the earlier full feature review.\n\n- Standards: no actionable findings.\n- Correctness: one low-severity Unicode query-length mismatch. The runtime counted UTF-16 units while the schema counts Unicode code points. Commit `b216d44` corrects the runtime check. Tests accepting 121 and 240 astral characters failed before the fix and pass afterward; a 241-character query remains rejected.\n- The reviewer checked the remediation and confirmed the finding resolved. No new foreground-dispatch or safety defect was found, and no delta-review findings remain open. This is not broader hardware qualification or production approval.\n\n## Remaining limits and release gates\n\nThe live tests establish Windows Notepad background typing, foreground modifier recovery and in-flight text cancellation. They do not qualify held modifier or mouse-button release during cancellation, all applications or display/window states, locked desktops/UAC, or macOS permissions and lifecycle. History still accumulates until normal compaction; caching behavior is unchanged.\n\nThe pinned CuaDriver remains approved for development only. Production publication requires separate explicit approval and a new CLI release version. Screen content can enter provider requests and saved sessions; GUI changes are outside file rollback. Local `/computer setup` verifies host-specific bundled CuaDriver payloads.\n\n## Latest work\n\n- Integrated master and the scoped baseline repairs from #118 without rewriting ancestry. Source packaging tests use inert fixtures rather than requiring native release archives.\n- Added optional `computer_apps.query` to filter named apps and window titles before pagination. In the same synthetic 139-app fixture, finding Notepad takes one call instead of three and returns 147 text characters instead of 8,699. Loaded tool definitions grow by 230 characters. These are payload and call-count measurements, not provider-token measurements.\n- Fixed a foreground shortcut failure reproduced live on Windows. The pinned driver's `hotkey` implementation routes XAML windows through background UIA before checking foreground mode. Eligible Windows foreground modifier shortcuts now use its existing `press_key` modifier route. The native runtime pin is unchanged.\n\n## Verification\n\n- Latest focused computer-use run: 109 tests across ten suites pass. The Unicode query fix also passes a rebuilt coding-agent/Node bundle and fresh first-request checks. Five offline package builds, the coding-agent Node bundle, and browser-on/off first-paint and first-request checks pass.\n- Earlier combined verification passed 391 tests across 31 files and eight archive/package tests. Seven public-name packages with real pinned native payloads passed relocated installation, OS/CPU selection, omitted-optional recovery and exact installer-lock checks on Windows x64. All three archives matched committed sizes and SHA-256 hashes. These packaging checks did not operate the desktop.\n- Separately authorized live Windows tests used the compiled registered computer tools and real pinned runtime in unsaved Notepad scratch documents. Background typing matched the expected 39-character phrase in the post-action image.\n- After a real background Ctrl+A failure and a fresh exact-window capture, the repaired foreground route visibly selected all 39 characters. A foreground new-tab shortcut then opened an empty scratch document without replacing the earlier text.\n- A 2,048-character foreground typing request was cancelled 86 ms after native RPC dispatch while the request was pending. The fresh screenshot showed six characters, proving partial delivery. The tool reported uncertain input and confirmed cleanup. The native process exited and the desktop lease released before a new workflow successfully captured the same window. Final shutdown stopped the new native process and released its lease too.\n- Ubuntu CI is not clean. At reviewed head `66e1a12`, the complete job log has exactly the same 98 failing test names across 24 suites as the #118 baseline, with zero new failures. Agent passes 181 tests, AI passes 623 with 760 skips, and coding-agent passes 2815 with 98 failures and 55 skips. Broader Ubuntu cleanup remains outside this update. CI for the subsequent Unicode boundary fix is separate from those completed results.\n\n## Independent delta review\n\nA fresh heavy read-only reviewer examined the named-app discovery and Windows foreground-shortcut changes from `217a98e` through `66e1a12`, separately from the earlier full feature review.\n\n- Standards: no actionable findings.\n- Correctness: one low-severity Unicode query-length mismatch. The runtime counted UTF-16 units while the schema counts Unicode code points. Commit `b216d44` corrects the runtime check. Tests accepting 121 and 240 astral characters failed before the fix and pass afterward; a 241-character query remains rejected.\n- The reviewer checked the remediation and confirmed the finding resolved. No new foreground-dispatch or safety defect was found, and no delta-review findings remain open. This is not broader hardware qualification or production approval.\n\n## Remaining limits and release gates\n\nThe live tests establish Windows Notepad background typing, foreground modifier recovery and in-flight text cancellation. They do not qualify held modifier or mouse-button release during cancellation, all applications or display/window states, locked desktops/UAC, or macOS permissions and lifecycle. The test runner called registered computer tools directly; it was not an autonomous provider-driven agent benchmark.\n\nCursor animation and screenshot-history pruning remain deferred. History still accumulates until normal compaction; caching behavior is unchanged.\n\nThe pinned CuaDriver remains approved for development only. Production publication requires separate explicit approval and a new CLI release version. Screen content can enter provider requests and saved sessions; GUI changes are outside file rollback. No installed CLI was changed. This update does not merge or publish a release.\n\nImplemented and validated with agent assistance in lunR. PR updated by GPT-6 Astra in lunR.\n",

      "patch": "@@ -0,0 +1,242 @@\n+# Image-only computer use\n+\n+This dev-channel integration combines stable lunR 0.2.21 with image-only computer\n+use. Offline builds, focused automated tests, local scripted-provider startup\n+checks, and isolated package installation pass. No live desktop capture or input,\n+native runtime launch, or remote inference ran. Stable production publication\n+remains blocked. Smooth cursor animation is not included.\n+\n+The dev package is `@ashx-j/lunr-dev`, with command `lunr-dev` and update command\n+`lunr-dev update`. Stable `@ashx-j/lunr` and `lunr` remain separate. Both commands\n+share `~/.lunr/agent` credentials, settings, and sessions.\n+\n+## Setup and permissions\n+\n+Run `/computer setup` in the local lunR terminal. Setup verifies and installs the\n+bundled runtime without downloading code, capturing the screen, or operating an\n+application. It is unavailable in headless and gateway sessions.\n+\n+Windows needs an active, unlocked desktop. On Apple Silicon macOS, setup prints\n+the exact installed `CuaDriver.app` path. Add that app to Accessibility and\n+Screen & System Audio Recording in System Settings > Privacy & Security, then\n+restart lunR. Older macOS versions call the second grant Screen Recording.\n+Only the user can grant these permissions. Setup leaves an existing\n+`/Applications/CuaDriver.app` alone.\n+\n+Computer use and Allow foreground control default to on. Windows x64/arm64 and\n+Apple Silicon expose `computer_load`; detailed tools load on demand. Linux and\n+Intel macOS have no native discovery tool. All computer tools except release\n+require an image-capable model. There is no text-only accessibility fallback.\n+Gateway sessions operate the gateway host, not the chat client's device.\n+\n+Manual approves observation and input. `computer_end` releases without approval.\n+Plan allows relevant observation and release, but blocks mutation. Auto allows\n+requested, implied, or necessary GUI work without lunR per-call prompts. In\n+Yolo, ask before introducing GUI work into an otherwise non-GUI task. These\n+intent rules are agent guidance, not a natural-language authorization classifier.\n+\n+Prefer background window input. Foreground window input requires a verified\n+background failure and a fresh image. Desktop input requires `desktop=true` and\n+`foreground=true`. Disabling foreground control blocks desktop input, foreground\n+window input, launch, and window management. An application can still change its\n+own focus after background input.\n+\n+Native tools are excluded from children and refuse child execution. Children\n+with shell access are not OS-sandboxed. No raw driver administration, update,\n+recording, or permission tool is exposed.\n+\n+## Observe, act, inspect\n+\n+1. Use `computer_apps` for app identities or windows for a PID. Results allowlist\n+   at most 50 rows and truncate titles to 240 characters. Pass `next_offset` as\n+   `offset` with the same PID selection to retrieve more apps or windows. Lists\n+   refresh per call, so changing native order can shift page boundaries. PID zero\n+   identifies an installed app that is not running. Window `bounds` are native\n+   geometry, not screenshot coordinates.\n+2. Use `computer_observe` with an exact `pid` and `window_id`, or `desktop=true`.\n+   The result contains one image and a short coordinate/token record.\n+3. Choose one action from that image. Pass its `observation` token and coordinates\n+   in the returned image. The workflow applies the mapping; do not scale twice.\n+4. Inspect the post-action image before continuing. The tool executes one action\n+   and captures the same target once. It never polls or retries input internally.\n+5. Call `computer_end` when finished.\n+\n+The token lasts 30 seconds, belongs to one exact target, and permits one action.\n+Every new observation invalidates the previous token before capture. Failed,\n+cancelled, or malformed captures issue no token. Old tokens cannot be replayed,\n+including after a successful action returns a new image.\n+\n+Supported input is single, double, and right click with modifiers, a complete\n+press-drag-release gesture, scrolling at image coordinates, Unicode text, and\n+keys or modifier shortcuts. Window text/keys can use image coordinates or the\n+observed focused field. Desktop text/keys use the observed focused field only;\n+change focus with a separate grounded click.\n+\n+`computer_window` supports `frame` in native window-bounds units and `focus` on\n+an exact observed window. Minimize/restore uses a grounded image click on a\n+visible control. The pinned driver has no portable minimize/restore RPC.\n+`computer_launch` returns bounded app metadata, not an inferred input target;\n+capture an exact window before acting.\n+\n+A successful transport or a changed image does not prove the intended application\n+effect. Results preserve partial/unverifiable outcomes and bounded refusal codes.\n+When input returns but its post-image fails, the tool reports possible effects\n+and stops the workflow. Capture again before deciding; never repeat input blindly.\n+After an unchanged post-image, the same action against identical captured pixels\n+is refused. Click signatures normalize omitted left-button/single-click/empty\n+modifier defaults and modifier order. Three consecutive unchanged full observations\n+stop polling in that workflow. Crops are explicit requests, not an automatic retry loop.\n+\n+Partial typing retains validated `requested_chars`, `delivered_chars`, `retryable`,\n+and `retry_from_character` when supplied by the driver. Counts must be safe integers\n+within the submitted text's Unicode code-point length, capped at 20000; the retry\n+index must equal the delivered count. The index is zero-based in Unicode code\n+points, not UTF-16 units. Verify the field in a fresh image before considering a\n+remaining suffix. `retryable` is driver advice, not permission or proof that\n+repeating input is safe. The workflow never retries typing automatically.\n+\n+## Image contract and cost limits\n+\n+Window capture requests `include_accessibility_tree:false` and\n+`include_screenshot:true`. Neither native accessibility trees nor duplicate raw\n+JSON reach the model. The macOS driver still reads minimal native accessibility\n+facts for window identity and background-input safety. Windows window discovery\n+can use UIA as a fallback. Image-only describes application observation sent to\n+the model, not the removal of every native accessibility API call.\n+\n+Window capture requests a 2560-pixel maximum. The runtime can impose a lower\n+configured ceiling, so this is not a promised capture resolution. The workflow\n+checks actual PNG dimensions against native screenshot metadata and rejects\n+invalid frames. Primary-desktop capture is tree-free and uses the native PNG.\n+Desktop coordinates map back to that PNG once; macOS `scale_factor` is not an\n+additional multiplier.\n+\n+Returned images have a maximum 1280-pixel edge, one million pixels, and 1.5 MiB\n+of base64 payload. The existing image processor bounds dimensions and encoding\n+size. The workflow refuses images it cannot decode or map. Source PNGs also have\n+allocation limits. These are engineering bounds, not measured token savings.\n+\n+For small text or controls, request `crop:{x,y,width,height}` with the latest\n+observation token. The rectangle uses that returned image's pixels. The workflow\n+captures fresh pixels, maps the rectangle into the full capture, and sends only\n+the crop. Its record gives the source dimensions, crop offset, and separate x/y\n+ratios. Changed source dimensions or reported window bounds reject the crop;\n+request a full image again. Cropping cannot recover detail absent from the native\n+capture. Post-action captures return the full target so dialogs outside a crop\n+remain visible.\n+\n+Saved sessions retain the returned screenshots. Provider-facing screenshot\n+history also accumulates until normal compaction. This change does not prune\n+user images, rewrite saved sessions, or implement a generic rolling history\n+filter. A targeted `context` hook could remove old computer screenshots while\n+leaving sessions intact, but a rolling cutoff changes an earlier prompt prefix\n+and can invalidate cached input. That tradeoff needs approved provider measurements\n+before adopting a retention policy. Image-only is not automatically cheaper than\n+text. Current cost controls bound each new payload, remove tree/JSON duplication,\n+and combine one action with its post-image.\n+\n+## Cursor status\n+\n+Cursor animation remains a separate native-runtime decision. The inherited\n+runtime launch still uses `--no-overlay`. Upstream Windows drag animation uses a\n+timer separate from actual input, and desktop pointer movement can teleport.\n+This branch does not claim smooth actual-cursor motion or synchronized drag\n+feedback. Any eventual animation must stay local, preserve full gestures and\n+cancellation, and send zero intermediate frames to the model.\n+\n+## Ownership and cancellation\n+\n+An OS-account lease spans observations and actions, independent of settings\n+profiles. Competing workflows receive busy rather than queueing. Calls within a\n+workflow serialize. One cross-process lock covers creation, atomic replacement,\n+and deletion of the owner record. A separate lock protects runtime installation.\n+A live owner is not displaced because its heartbeat is late.\n+\n+After MCP initialization and before any driver tool dispatch, the adapter records\n+the transport PID and, on macOS, daemon PID. Missing identities or failed lease\n+updates refuse dispatch. Recovery requires both owner and recorded runtimes to\n+have exited. PID reuse and malformed owner records fail closed. A crash during\n+initialization can leave an unrecorded idle runtime that received no input.\n+\n+Release, cancellation, agent end, settings changes, and session shutdown close\n+the owned runtime before releasing the lease. Queued work cannot survive\n+cancellation. Unconfirmed shutdown retains ownership. Cancellation cannot retract\n+already delivered input, and forced termination does not prove held input was\n+released. Driver-internal helper lifetime and held-input cancellation still need\n+native acceptance.\n+\n+Gateway cron creates fresh permission contexts with the configured default mode,\n+without gateway approvals or its approval handler. Missing approval blocks calls.\n+Session shutdown precedes disposal, even after partial extension binding failure.\n+TUI cron continues to use its live permission context.\n+\n+## Runtime and distribution\n+\n+The development pin is [CuaDriver 0.28.1](https://github.com/trycua/cua/releases/tag/cua-driver-rs-v0.28.1),\n+source `d8028a7943087ee258dc1b4d19dc12a7cd27669c`. Archive identities and approval\n+are in `scripts/computer-use-release.json`; `release.generated.ts` derives from\n+it. The upstream MIT license is under `native/computer-use`. No runtime pin or\n+native binary changed in the image-only workflow work.\n+\n+The runtime resolves the host's optional payload package or matching archive\n+beside a standalone executable. It verifies the archive, extracts a fresh\n+reference tree, and checks cached files/helpers against it. Redirected paths and\n+escaping symlinks are refused. Installers do not overwrite an existing runtime.\n+After confirming all owned processes stopped, an inactive cache can be removed\n+for reinstallation. Runtime code is never downloaded at first use.\n+\n+Windows uses system `tar.exe` and an isolated `mcp --direct --embedded\n+--no-overlay` process. A hidden system PowerShell metadata probe refuses session\n+zero, disconnected sessions, and inaccessible/non-Default input desktops. It\n+never switches desktops. Both platforms isolate profiles, strip inherited\n+`CUA_*`, set standard permission mode, and disable telemetry/update checks.\n+\n+macOS preserves the unchanged signed app at its stable lunR-owned path, verifies\n+its signature with `codesign --verify --deep --strict`, and launches that exact\n+path through `open -n -g -W -a`. A private HOME, socket, stdin FIFO, and\n+`--parent-liveness-stdio` isolate daemon state and lifetime. Shutdown uses the\n+private PID-bound endpoint and waits for the app to exit. No re-signing occurs.\n+\n+Release staging creates exact-version host-specific optional payload packages.\n+They contain unchanged archives and no install scripts. Workspace manifests keep\n+unpublished payload dependencies out. Standalone asset copying selects one\n+opaque archive. Stable publication remains gated on production approval and a\n+new CLI version. This integration retains dev-channel CLI naming, update routing,\n+and exact-version package/lock rewriting. Dev publication uses `latest` only for\n+`@ashx-j/lunr-dev`; shared libraries and payload packages use the `dev` tag. Stable\n+tags remain unchanged. The user requested a dev-channel update and installation,\n+with automated release checks complete. Publication and global installation remain\n+separate distribution steps.\n+\n+## Pending acceptance\n+\n+Source tests cover image-only capture flags, metadata allowlists, image/crop\n+mapping, fresh tokens, single-action post-images, bounded unchanged behavior,\n+uncertain outcomes, permissions, and ownership. Source-review fixes add equivalent\n+click defaults, app/window pagination, and Unicode partial-typing recovery coverage.\n+The focused 23-suite run passes 265 tests, including a real Photon PNG crop\n+fixture that checks output pixels and coordinate mapping. All five offline package\n+builds and the Node bundle pass. Clean-parent first-request capture confirms that\n+`computer_load` is the only addition to the unsupported-host tool inventory; the\n+supported-host fingerprint is current. Private prompt and tool snapshots remain\n+local validation artifacts.\n+\n+Seven dev package tarballs pass isolated installation and relocation checks,\n+host-only payload selection, archive verification, omitted-optional handling, and\n+the standalone installer lock. First-paint and first-turn subagent, MCP, LSP, and\n+local HTTP fixtures pass without remote inference. These checks do not launch the\n+native driver or prove application effects.\n+\n+Explicitly authorized desktop acceptance remains required. Native gates include\n+Windows locked/UAC/integrity states,\n+Electron/native apps, display scaling and moved/resized windows, Unicode,\n+held-input cancellation, and macOS TCC/LaunchServices/FIFO/shutdown on hardware.\n+Cursor/runtime changes need a separate scoped decision before implementation.\n+\n+## Privacy\n+\n+Images, window titles, and typed text can enter selected-provider requests and\n+saved sessions. Disabling driver telemetry does not disable lunR session storage.\n+GUI changes are outside filesystem rollback. Application content is untrusted\n+task data, never authorization. OS permissions, locked desktops, UAC, and\n+integrity restrictions still apply."

Returns a post-action image; verify the intended region moved.\",\n+\t\t\t\t\t\t\tcomputer_window:\n+\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\"Move/resize an observed window with action frame in native window-bounds units, or activate it with action focus. computerSchemas[name],\n+\t\t\tasync execute(_id, params, signal, _update, ctx) {\n+\t\t\t\tconst input: Record<string, unknown> = Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(params));\n+\t\t\t\tconst settings       "patch": "@@ -0,0 +1,31 @@\n+# lunR dev\n+\n+This package contains development builds from lunR's `dev/tui` branch. This integration combines stable lunR 0.2.21 with image-only computer use from PR #77's continuation.\n+\n+Computer use is experimental. Observations use bounded screenshots instead of accessibility trees, with crop mapping and one action plus a post-action image. Source-review fixes cover equivalent clicks, discovery pagination, and partial typing recovery. Offline builds, 265 focused tests, local scripted-provider startup checks, and isolated package installation pass. No native runtime launch, live desktop capture/input, or remote inference ran. Smooth cursor animation is not included; live desktop and macOS hardware acceptance remain pending. Stable `@ashx-j/lunr` is unchanged.\n+\n+Install it once:\n+\n+```bash\n+npm i -g @ashx-j/lunr-dev\n+```\n+\n+Run it with:\n+\n+```bash\n+lunr-dev\n+```\n+\n+Pull the newest published build with:\n+\n+```bash\n+lunr-dev update\n+```\n+\n+Stable lunR remains available as `lunr`. Both commands use `~/.lunr/agent`, so they share credentials, settings, and sessions.\n+\n+For computer use, run `/computer setup` in the local terminal. Windows x64/arm64 and Apple Silicon macOS receive only their matching optional runtime package. Keep optional dependencies enabled during installation. Screen and application content can enter model requests and saved sessions. GUI actions are outside file rollback.\n+\n+See [computer-use setup and limitations](https://github.com/ashx-j/lunR/blob/dev/tui/packages/coding-agent/docs/computer-use.md).\n+\n+For full documentation, see [the lunR README](https://github.com/ashx-j/lunR/blob/master/packages/coding-agent/README.md)."

      "patch": "@@ -0,0 +1,242 @@\n+# Image-only computer use\n+\n+This dev-channel integration combines stable lunR 0.2.21 with image-only computer\n+use. Offline builds, focused automated tests, local scripted-provider startup\n+checks, and isolated package installation pass. No live desktop capture or input,\n+native runtime launch, or remote inference ran. Stable production publication\n+remains blocked. Smooth cursor animation is not included.\n+\n+The dev package is `@ashx-j/lunr-dev`, with command `lunr-dev` and update command\n+`lunr-dev update`. Stable `@ashx-j/lunr` and `lunr` remain separate. Both commands\n+share `~/.lunr/agent` credentials, settings, and sessions.\n+\n+## Setup and permissions\n+\n+Run `/computer setup` in the local lunR terminal. Setup verifies and installs the\n+bundled runtime without downloading code, capturing the screen, or operating an\n+application. It is unavailable in headless and gateway sessions.\n+\n+Windows needs an active, unlocked desktop. On Apple Silicon macOS, setup prints\n+the exact installed `CuaDriver.app` path. Add that app to Accessibility and\n+Screen & System Audio Recording in System Settings > Privacy & Security, then\n+restart lunR. Older macOS versions call the second grant Screen Recording.\n+Only the user can grant these permissions. Setup leaves an existing\n+`/Applications/CuaDriver.app` alone.\n+\n+Computer use and Allow foreground control default to on. Windows x64/arm64 and\n+Apple Silicon expose `computer_load`; detailed tools load on demand. Linux and\n+Intel macOS have no native discovery tool. All computer tools except release\n+require an image-capable model. There is no text-only accessibility fallback.\n+Gateway sessions operate the gateway host, not the chat client's device.\n+\n+Manual approves observation and input. `computer_end` releases without approval.\n+Plan allows relevant observation and release, but blocks mutation. Auto allows\n+requested, implied, or necessary GUI work without lunR per-call prompts. In\n+Yolo, ask before introducing GUI work into an otherwise non-GUI task. These\n+intent rules are agent guidance, not a natural-language authorization classifier.\n+\n+Prefer background window input. Foreground window input requires a verified\n+background failure and a fresh image. Desktop input requires `desktop=true` and\n+`foreground=true`. Disabling foreground control blocks desktop input, foreground\n+window input, launch, and window management. An application can still change its\n+own focus after background input.\n+\n+Native tools are excluded from children and refuse child execution. Children\n+with shell access are not OS-sandboxed. No raw driver administration, update,\n+recording, or permission tool is exposed.\n+\n+## Observe, act, inspect\n+\n+1. Use `computer_apps` for app identities or windows for a PID. Results allowlist\n+   at most 50 rows and truncate titles to 240 characters. Pass `next_offset` as\n+   `offset` with the same PID selection to retrieve more apps or windows. Lists\n+   refresh per call, so changing native order can shift page boundaries. PID zero\n+   identifies an installed app that is not running. Window `bounds` are native\n+   geometry, not screenshot coordinates.\n+2. Use `computer_observe` with an exact `pid` and `window_id`, or `desktop=true`.\n+   The result contains one image and a short coordinate/token record.\n+3. Choose one action from that image. Pass its `observation` token and coordinates\n+   in the returned image. The workflow applies the mapping; do not scale twice.\n+4. Inspect the post-action image before continuing. The tool executes one action\n+   and captures the same target once. It never polls or retries input internally.\n+5. Call `computer_end` when finished.\n+\n+The token lasts 30 seconds, belongs to one exact target, and permits one action.\n+Every new observation invalidates the previous token before capture. Failed,\n+cancelled, or malformed captures issue no token. Old tokens cannot be replayed,\n+including after a successful action returns a new image.\n+\n+Supported input is single, double, and right click with modifiers, a complete\n+press-drag-release gesture, scrolling at image coordinates, Unicode text, and\n+keys or modifier shortcuts. Window text/keys can use image coordinates or the\n+observed focused field. Desktop text/keys use the observed focused field only;\n+change focus with a separate grounded click.\n+\n+`computer_window` supports `frame` in native window-bounds units and `focus` on\n+an exact observed window. Minimize/restore uses a grounded image click on a\n+visible control. The pinned driver has no portable minimize/restore RPC.\n+`computer_launch` returns bounded app metadata, not an inferred input target;\n+capture an exact window before acting.\n+\n+A successful transport or a changed image does not prove the intended application\n+effect. Results preserve partial/unverifiable outcomes and bounded refusal codes.\n+When input returns but its post-image fails, the tool reports possible effects\n+and stops the workflow. Capture again before deciding; never repeat input blindly.\n+After an unchanged post-image, the same action against identical captured pixels\n+is refused. Click signatures normalize omitted left-button/single-click/empty\n+modifier defaults and modifier order. Three consecutive unchanged full observations\n+stop polling in that workflow. Crops are explicit requests, not an automatic retry loop.\n+\n+Partial typing retains validated `requested_chars`, `delivered_chars`, `retryable`,\n+and `retry_from_character` when supplied by the driver. Counts must be safe integers\n+within the submitted text's Unicode code-point length, capped at 20000; the retry\n+index must equal the delivered count. The index is zero-based in Unicode code\n+points, not UTF-16 units. Verify the field in a fresh image before considering a\n+remaining suffix. `retryable` is driver advice, not permission or proof that\n+repeating input is safe. The workflow never retries typing automatically.\n+\n+## Image contract and cost limits\n+\n+Window capture requests `include_accessibility_tree:false` and\n+`include_screenshot:true`. Neither native accessibility trees nor duplicate raw\n+JSON reach the model. The macOS driver still reads minimal native accessibility\n+facts for window identity and background-input safety. Windows window discovery\n+can use UIA as a fallback. Image-only describes application observation sent to\n+the model, not the removal of every native accessibility API call.\n+\n+Window capture requests a 2560-pixel maximum. The runtime can impose a lower\n+configured ceiling, so this is not a promised capture resolution. The workflow\n+checks actual PNG dimensions against native screenshot metadata and rejects\n+invalid frames. Primary-desktop capture is tree-free and uses the native PNG.\n+Desktop coordinates map back to that PNG once; macOS `scale_factor` is not an\n+additional multiplier.\n+\n+Returned images have a maximum 1280-pixel edge, one million pixels, and 1.5 MiB\n+of base64 payload. The existing image processor bounds dimensions and encoding\n+size. The workflow refuses images it cannot decode or map. Source PNGs also have\n+allocation limits. These are engineering bounds, not measured token savings.\n+\n+For small text or controls, request `crop:{x,y,width,height}` with the latest\n+observation token. The rectangle uses that returned image's pixels. The workflow\n+captures fresh pixels, maps the rectangle into the full capture, and sends only\n+the crop. Its record gives the source dimensions, crop offset, and separate x/y\n+ratios. Changed source dimensions or reported window bounds reject the crop;\n+request a full image again. Cropping cannot recover detail absent from the native\n+capture. Post-action captures return the full target so dialogs outside a crop\n+remain visible.\n+\n+Saved sessions retain the returned screenshots. Provider-facing screenshot\n+history also accumulates until normal compaction. This change does not prune\n+user images, rewrite saved sessions, or implement a generic rolling history\n+filter. A targeted `context` hook could remove old computer screenshots while\n+leaving sessions intact, but a rolling cutoff changes an earlier prompt prefix\n+and can invalidate cached input. That tradeoff needs approved provider measurements\n+before adopting a retention policy. Image-only is not automatically cheaper than\n+text. Current cost controls bound each new payload, remove tree/JSON duplication,\n+and combine one action with its post-image.\n+\n+## Cursor status\n+\n+Cursor animation remains a separate native-runtime decision. The inherited\n+runtime launch still uses `--no-overlay`. Upstream Windows drag animation uses a\n+timer separate from actual input, and desktop pointer movement can teleport.\n+This branch does not claim smooth actual-cursor motion or synchronized drag\n+feedback. Any eventual animation must stay local, preserve full gestures and\n+cancellation, and send zero intermediate frames to the model.\n+\n+## Ownership and cancellation\n+\n+An OS-account lease spans observations and actions, independent of settings\n+profiles. Competing workflows receive busy rather than queueing. Calls within a\n+workflow serialize. One cross-process lock covers creation, atomic replacement,\n+and deletion of the owner record. A separate lock protects runtime installation.\n+A live owner is not displaced because its heartbeat is late.\n+\n+After MCP initialization and before any driver tool dispatch, the adapter records\n+the transport PID and, on macOS, daemon PID. Missing identities or failed lease\n+updates refuse dispatch. Recovery requires both owner and recorded runtimes to\n+have exited. PID reuse and malformed owner records fail closed. A crash during\n+initialization can leave an unrecorded idle runtime that received no input.\n+\n+Release, cancellation, agent end, settings changes, and session shutdown close\n+the owned runtime before releasing the lease. Queued work cannot survive\n+cancellation. Unconfirmed shutdown retains ownership. Cancellation cannot retract\n+already delivered input, and forced termination does not prove held input was\n+released. Driver-internal helper lifetime and held-input cancellation still need\n+native acceptance.\n+\n+Gateway cron creates fresh permission contexts with the configured default mode,\n+without gateway approvals or its approval handler. Missing approval blocks calls.\n+Session shutdown precedes disposal, even after partial extension binding failure.\n+TUI cron continues to use its live permission context.\n+\n+## Runtime and distribution\n+\n+The development pin is [CuaDriver 0.28.1](https://github.com/trycua/cua/releases/tag/cua-driver-rs-v0.28.1),\n+source `d8028a7943087ee258dc1b4d19dc12a7cd27669c`. Archive identities and approval\n+are in `scripts/computer-use-release.json`; `release.generated.ts` derives from\n+it. The upstream MIT license is under `native/computer-use`. No runtime pin or\n+native binary changed in the image-only workflow work.\n+\n+The runtime resolves the host's optional payload package or matching archive\n+beside a standalone executable. It verifies the archive, extracts a fresh\n+reference tree, and checks cached files/helpers against it. Redirected paths and\n+escaping symlinks are refused. Installers do not overwrite an existing runtime.\n+After confirming all owned processes stopped, an inactive cache can be removed\n+for reinstallation. Runtime code is never downloaded at first use.\n+\n+Windows uses system `tar.exe` and an isolated `mcp --direct --embedded\n+--no-overlay` process. A hidden system PowerShell metadata probe refuses session\n+zero, disconnected sessions, and inaccessible/non-Default input desktops. It\n+never switches desktops. Both platforms isolate profiles, strip inherited\n+`CUA_*`, set standard permission mode, and disable telemetry/update checks.\n+\n+macOS preserves the unchanged signed app at its stable lunR-owned path, verifies\n+its signature with `codesign --verify --deep --strict`, and launches that exact\n+path through `open -n -g -W -a`. A private HOME, socket, stdin FIFO, and\n+`--parent-liveness-stdio` isolate daemon state and lifetime. Shutdown uses the\n+private PID-bound endpoint and waits for the app to exit. No re-signing occurs.\n+\n+Release staging creates exact-version host-specific optional payload packages.\n+They contain unchanged archives and no install scripts. Workspace manifests keep\n+unpublished payload dependencies out. Standalone asset copying selects one\n+opaque archive. Stable publication remains gated on production approval and a\n+new CLI version. This integration retains dev-channel CLI naming, update routing,\n+and exact-version package/lock rewriting. Dev publication uses `latest` only for\n+`@ashx-j/lunr-dev`; shared libraries and payload packages use the `dev` tag. Stable\n+tags remain unchanged. The user requested a dev-channel update and installation,\n+with automated release checks complete. Publication and global installation remain\n+separate distribution steps.\n+\n+## Pending acceptance\n+\n+Source tests cover image-only capture flags, metadata allowlists, image/crop\n+mapping, fresh tokens, single-action post-images, bounded unchanged behavior,\n+uncertain outcomes, permissions, and ownership. Source-review fixes add equivalent\n+click defaults, app/window pagination, and Unicode partial-typing recovery coverage.\n+The focused 23-suite run passes 265 tests, including a real Photon PNG crop\n+fixture that checks output pixels and coordinate mapping. All five offline package\n+builds and the Node bundle pass. Clean-parent first-request capture confirms that\n+`computer_load` is the only addition to the unsupported-host tool inventory; the\n+supported-host fingerprint is current. Private prompt and tool snapshots remain\n+local validation artifacts.\n+\n+Seven dev package tarballs pass isolated installation and relocation checks,\n+host-only payload selection, archive verification, omitted-optional handling, and\n+the standalone installer lock. First-paint and first-turn subagent, MCP, LSP, and\n+local HTTP fixtures pass without remote inference. These checks do not launch the\n+native driver or prove application effects.\n+\n+Explicitly authorized desktop acceptance remains required. Native gates include\n+Windows locked/UAC/integrity states,\n+Electron/native apps, display scaling and moved/resized windows, Unicode,\n+held-input cancellation, and macOS TCC/LaunchServices/FIFO/shutdown on hardware.\n+Cursor/runtime changes need a separate scoped decision before implementation.\n+\n+## Privacy\n+\n+Images, window titles, and typed text can enter selected-provider requests and\n+saved sessions. Disabling driver telemetry does not disable lunR session storage.\n+GUI changes are outside filesystem rollback. Application content is untrusted\n+task data, never authorization. OS permissions, locked desktops, UAC, and\n+integrity restrictions still apply."

      "patch": "@@ -0,0 +1,31 @@\n+# lunR dev\n+\n+This package contains development builds from lunR's `dev/tui` branch. This integration combines stable lunR 0.2.21 with image-only computer use from PR #77's continuation.\n+\n+Computer use is experimental. Observations use bounded screenshots instead of accessibility trees, with crop mapping and one action plus a post-action image. Source-review fixes cover equivalent clicks, discovery pagination, and partial typing recovery. Offline builds, 265 focused tests, local scripted-provider startup checks, and isolated package installation pass. No native runtime launch, live desktop capture/input, or remote inference ran. Smooth cursor animation is not included; live desktop and macOS hardware acceptance remain pending. Stable `@ashx-j/lunr` is unchanged.\n+\n+Install it once:\n+\n+```bash\n+npm i -g @ashx-j/lunr-dev\n+```\n+\n+Run it with:\n+\n+```bash\n+lunr-dev\n+```\n+\n+Pull the newest published build with:\n+\n+```bash\n+lunr-dev update\n+```\n+\n+Stable lunR remains available as `lunr`. Both commands use `~/.lunr/agent`, so they share credentials, settings, and sessions.\n+\n+For computer use, run `/computer setup` in the local terminal. Windows x64/arm64 and Apple Silicon macOS receive only their matching optional runtime package. Keep optional dependencies enabled during installation. Screen and application content can enter model requests and saved sessions. GUI actions are outside file rollback.\n+\n+See [computer-use setup and limitations](https://github.com/ashx-j/lunR/blob/dev/tui/packages/coding-agent/docs/computer-use.md).\n+\n+For full documentation, see [the lunR README](https://github.com/ashx-j/lunR/blob/master/packages/coding-agent/README.md)."

# publish-npm-dev.yml

name: Publish npm dev channel

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - "dev/tui"

permissions: {}

concurrency:
  group: publish-npm-dev
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  publish:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      id-token: write
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@11bd71901bbe5b1630ceea73d27597364c9af683 # v4.2.2
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Setup Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@39370e3970a6d050c480ffad4ff0ed4d3fdee5af # v4.1.0
        with:
          node-version: "22"
          registry-url: "https://registry.npmjs.org"
          cache: npm

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci --ignore-scripts

      - name: Build
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          npx tsgo -p packages/tui/tsconfig.build.json
          npx tsgo -p packages/ai/tsconfig.build.json
          npx tsgo -p packages/agent/tsconfig.build.json
          npm --prefix packages/coding-agent run build
          npx tsgo -p packages/orchestrator/tsconfig.build.json

      - name: Prepare pinned computer-use payloads
        run: |
          node scripts/download-computer-use-release.mjs "$RUNNER_TEMP/cua-release"
          node scripts/bundle-computer-use.mjs "$RUNNER_TEMP/cua-release"
          node scripts/generate-computer-use-manifest.mjs --check
          node --test scripts/check-computer-use-release.test.mjs scripts/computer-use-packages.test.mjs

      - name: Validate computer use and dev channel
        working-directory: packages/coding-agent
        run: npx vitest --run test/computer-*.test.ts test/lunr-npm-names.test.ts test/update-check.test.ts test/lunr-tab-title.test.ts

      - name: Verify first paint and first request
        run: node scripts/check-interactive-first-paint.mjs

      - name: Publish dev packages
        env:
          NODE_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          BASE_VERSION="$(node -p "require('./packages/coding-agent/package.json').version")"
          DEV_VERSION="${BASE_VERSION}-dev.${{ github.run_number }}.${{ github.run_attempt }}"
          node scripts/publish.mjs --channel dev --version "$DEV_VERSION"
